Both arms shared the same snapshot so the comparison is fair; with-skill agents compensated by consulting the live checkout the skill references.

eval-2 (guide-select) was the big discriminator: with the skill, a one-call find_by_meta solution targeting the real meta API; without it, a 74-line manual tm.ls loop reading a plain 'kind' attribute that would select nothing against the current repo's tikMeta_ JSON semantics.

eval-0 (prop-rig) did not discriminate on assertions (4/4 both arms): the repo's CLAUDE.md one-liner already keeps agents off raw cmds. The skill's visible effect was subtler quality: wrapper-object hygiene (parent=offset vs parent=offset.long_name), an explicit mesh argument, and constraints via the documented proxy escape hatch. Consider a sharper assertion or accept this eval as a regression guard.

eval-1 (mirror-chain): both arms correctly extended tik.maya's Joint rather than writing tool-level code - repo conventions are strong. The skill's margin was house-style: typed signature and @protected on the with-skill run, missing on the baseline.

Single run per configuration - variance is unknown; the stddev columns reflect across-eval spread, not repeat-run noise. Time and tokens are roughly equal between arms, so the skill adds capability at no measurable cost.

Side finding worth acting on regardless of the skill: the eval-2 baseline surfaced a real tik.maya bug - Plug resolves attributes by short name (plug.py _find_plug), raising RuntimeError on nodes with ambiguous short names.
